reasoning_summary: SOL is testing the 98-102 September floor after rejection near 124; the bull case requires holding 98 and reclaiming 107 toward 112/116, while the bear case on losing 96 exposes 92/90.
BTC is bouncing off a rising trendline with RSI reset; the bull case targets 84,000-86,000 if 82,000 is reclaimed, while the bear case risks 78,000-76,000 if 79,000 breaks.

The author claims that when the share of Bitcoin held for more than 18 months rises and then starts to decline, a strong rally usually follows, indicating the crypto market is quietly preparing for its next rally.

Bitcoin is down 4.2% in October versus its historical average gain, US buyers have stepped back, Coinbase Premium is negative and at a June low, and short-term trader paper profits have fallen from 33% to 8%, with support near the 365-day MA at $77.6K and average cost basis at $74K.
A backtested BTC strategy buys when the 30-day RSI of entities in profit crosses above its threshold; since July 2023 its worst drawdown was 20% versus 53% for holding.

Hyperliquid whales have flipped to net short BTC for the first time since March after previously longing the bottom; the author asks whether this signals an early deeper pullback or a potential squeeze if price turns higher.

BTC has been beating the S&P 500, winning more trading days than it lost over recent weeks despite a weak June, and this outperformance could become reflexive as investors rotate into the strongest asset class.
Whales are dumping SOL; three wallets possibly controlled by the same whale moved 482,228 SOL ($49.17M) over the past three days to sell, with 171,430 SOL ($17.3M) already deposited into exchanges.
Galaxy Digital says the bear market ended in June and Bitcoin is in an accumulation phase before a price surge.
